approach: Add `check_behavior_test_reading` to crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs, gated by the existing `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`. Wire it as one `step!` line directly after `step!(check_code_survey(reading))` in checks.rs. Each of the four parts (a)-(d) is met either by its labelled clause (`Gate order:`, `Existing code:`, `Record kind:`, `Direct check:`) or by markers in a `Code survey:` assumption. Revision 5 changes only the survey-marker route and part (d). (1) The survey markers for (a) and (b) now match what past surveys were told to write, so neither a stop-gate phrase nor a reuse word is required on the survey route. The stop-gate phrase stays only for the labelled `Gate order:` clause. (2) Part (d) no longer maps criterion numbers to `Direct check:` text: that machinery is dropped, together with the stale-number logic and the range-form code. (d) asks for one direct-check clause or survey sentence with a function-like identifier, unless every behavior criterion is routine. (3) The open question is non-blocking. (4) The reader guide is reworded, the section is measured, and raising the 3045 baseline and the 3150 cap by the measured growth is the planned path. A unit test runs the check on this job's own reading, quoted verbatim, as a real-reading counterexample check. The negation, skip-switch, command-removal, routine-criterion and one-error design from revision 4 is kept. status.rs, verify.rs and replay.rs stay unchanged and are named in `unchanged_planned_files`. No prompt file, record, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow is touched.

decisions.choice: Each part (a)-(d) is met by its labelled clause OR by markers in a `Code survey:` assumption, and the markers are matched to what the reader guide already asks for. (a) labelled `Gate order:` body: at least two broad identifiers AND a stop-gate phrase (`stop gate`, `stops at`, `stops after`, `stop at`, `stops before`). (a) survey route: one sentence of a `Code survey:` holding `entry point`, `entry via` or `order`, plus at least two broad identifiers; no stop phrase required. (b) labelled: an `Existing code:` assumption with a crates/ path the job does not create (`names_existing_path`, surveys.rs:1341) and a broad identifier. (b) survey route: a `Code survey:` sentence holding a crates/ path the job does not create plus a broad identifier; no reuse word required. (c) labelled `Record kind:` body satisfying `names_record_evidence`, or `none` while no deliverable satisfies `is_record_or_data_deliverable`; survey route: a `Code survey:` satisfying `names_record_evidence` or holding `no record` or `adds no record`. (d) labelled: a `Direct check:` body with a function-like identifier after command removal; survey route: a `Code survey:` holding `measured directly` or `direct check` plus a function-like identifier anywhere in the same assumption.
decisions.reason: Finding 1. The guide (reader.rs:356-359) asks for 'the entry point, and the order in which resolution and probing run', for record validation, and for 'how the property is measured directly'. It never asks for a stop gate or the word reuse, so those markers would newly refuse almost every past code behavior reading. On this route the check cannot show that a stop gate was stated; it only shows entry or order wording and two real identifiers. Doc comment and CHANGELOG say so: the survey route for (a) does not check the stop gate, and the survey route for (b) only checks that the survey names an existing path and function. The labelled clauses stay the precise route; the error text asks for the labelled form. The share of newly refused readings is still not measured (records/ is absent from the snapshot). It should be lower than with the revision-4 markers, but it is not shown to be under 35%. Only `loop_replay` and the verification replay measure it, and the plan loosens nothing after they run (AC4). Verified against this job's own reading: its `Code survey:` bullet holds `entry via check_reading_text` and identifiers such as `check_code_survey` and `names_record_evidence` in its first sentence; it names crates/ paths the job does not create; it says the change adds no record and names `check_record_file`; and it says 'measured directly' and names `check_reading_text`. It therefore meets (a)-(d) by markers.

rejected.why: Finding 1: the guide never asks for them, so the marker route does not lower the share, and this job's own reading would be refused.

decisions.choice: Part (c) and the record contradiction. `Record kind: none` beside a deliverable that satisfies `is_record_or_data_deliverable` is refused as a contradiction naming (c) and the file. The new check does not re-test survey evidence: `check_code_survey` (surveys.rs:217-230) runs first and refuses a record deliverable whose survey lacks evidence. The new check does not carry a round-trip-deliverable-path branch.

AC3's 'no accepted record kind and no round-trip test deliverable' is refused in two places: `check_code_survey` for a survey without evidence (a corpus case pins it) and the new check when `Record kind: none` meets a record file. A broad identifier is a token with `_` or `::`, a word directly followed by `()`, or a backticked single token; a token with `/` or a file extension never counts. Single backticked words such as `replay` (replay.rs:365) stay valid entry points.

decisions.choice: Part (d) is checked once per reading, not per criterion (finding 2). The check requires (i) a `Direct check:` body or a `Code survey:` that holds `measured directly` or `direct check`, and (ii) a function-like identifier (`_`, `::` or `name()`) in that same body or assumption, found after command removal. All criterion-number code (`criterion_numbers`, found/covered/missing lists, stale-number tests, the `criteria-range-form` corpus case) is dropped. The check does not map direct-check text to individual criteria; the doc comment and CHANGELOG say so, and say that the critic and verifier judge whether each property has its own check. Command removal strips backtick spans starting `cargo ` and the word `cargo` to the end of its clause, so a cargo command never counts. A backtick span starting `athena <subcommand>` counts when the text of some non-routine behavior criterion contains that subcommand word (for example `athena check-reading` for criterion 5 of this request); any other `athena ` span is removed. Skip switches: the closed list `skip_probe`, `ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, and upper-case tokens starting `ATHENA_NO_` or `ATHENA_SKIP_` (case-sensitive); a lower-case name merely containing `skip_`, such as `skip_note` (checks.rs:271), never matches. Internal-helper phrases: `internal helper`, `private helper`, `stand-in`, `through a helper`, `via a helper`. A non-negated match refuses. The scan covers `Direct check:` bodies and, on the survey route, the sentence of the survey holding the marker.
decisions.reason: Finding 2: the survey route met (d) for all criteria at once, so the per-number machinery would rarely run and cost a stale-number failure mode. Dropping it makes both routes equal and the code smaller. The cost, stated as a limit, is that one function-like identifier satisfies (d) for several criteria. The `athena <subcommand>` rule keeps CLI-output criteria checkable by running the binary, and `cargo test` runs measure nothing about the property so they stay refused. The reading checks read the Reading only (surveys.rs:310-311), so the switch list cannot be checked against code; it is closed and the limit is stated.

rejected.why: Uneven checking: readers would take the loose route; extra code and a stale-number failure mode for no real gain.

decisions.choice: Negation. One shared `pub(super) const NEGATORS: [&str; 7]` (`no`, `not`, `never`, `without`, `nothing`, `nor`, `cannot`) with the existing `n't` and `n\u{2019}t` normalisation replaces the local list in `requires_existing_code_section` (surveys.rs:1359-1394) and is used by the new check. `rather than` negates; a bare `than` does not. For a match at token i, walk back over determiners and modifiers (`a`, `an`, `the`, `any`, `internal`, `private`, `helper`), at most one connective (`through`, `via`, `using`, `with`, `by`, `of`), and determiners again, and read token j. A negator at j negates. If j is `or` or `nor`, with one `,` directly before it counted as part of the joiner, and the token before the joiner is itself a match, return `negated` of that earlier match. `and` is not a joiner and a bare `,` does not carry negation. Accepted by test: `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, `without skip_probe, or ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, `not through skip_probe nor ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, `no skip_probe, no helper stand-in`, `not through a helper`, `without ATHENA_NO_PROBE`. Refused by test and pinned as limits: `no probe runs when skip_probe is set`, `faster than skip_probe`, `not through skip_probe and ATHENA_NO_PROBE is set`, `not through skip_probe, and ATHENA_NO_PROBE is set`, `without skip_probe and ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, `without skip_probe, ATHENA_NO_PROBE`.
decisions.reason: AC3 accepts a negated mention, and `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE` is an ordinary negated list. Dropping `and` and a bare comma as carriers makes the comma and no-comma forms behave the same and keeps a later switch in the refused cases visible. verify.rs:1261 holds a clause-level negator for verifier claims on different text and stays unchanged.

rejected.option: `and` carries negation
rejected.why: Accepts the no-comma form of a case the plan means to refuse.

rejected.option: Strict 'negator directly before the match'
rejected.why: Refuses `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE`.

rejected.option: Reuse verify.rs `is_negator`
rejected.why: Changes verify.rs; AC8 forbids unrelated changes.

decisions.choice: A criterion is routine, and needs no direct-check clause, when after stripping every whitespace token starting `-` and every token starting `athena-`, the remaining lower-cased alphanumeric words are all in the stop list (cargo, fmt, clippy, test, tests, check, pass, passes, passing, and, the, on, final, tree, still, all, locked, same, as, a, recorded, athena, workspace, warnings, targets, no, unrelated, behavior, changes, change, existing, run) and the criterion holds a pass word and one of fmt, clippy or test(s). When every behavior criterion is routine, (d) is not required. Parts (a)-(c) are still required.
decisions.reason: AC3 says a routine criterion needs no direct-check clause. Stripping flags and crate names avoids single-letter stop words for `-D warnings` and `-p`.

rejected.option: Add `d`, `p` and crate names to the stop list
rejected.why: Single letters let unrelated criteria through.

rejected.option: Skip the whole check when all behavior criteria are routine
rejected.why: AC2 still requires (a)-(c).
